text: Reading the state used to walk up the ancestor chain on every check, which added query overhead and needed caching. Propagation writes the state onto every descendant, so a read is a single-column comparison; writes do more work, asynchronously, in batches. The change and an outbox row commit in the same transaction, and StatePropagationCronWorker re-enqueues pending or stalled rows. A subgroup already deletion_scheduled stays deletion_scheduled, because a lower-precedence propagation never overwrites a higher one (doc/development/namespaces_state_propagation.md).
